facts.label: Source-risk mechanisms and downstream consequences
facts.text: - Revolver maturity. Evidence: the 10-Q states "$220 million in revolving commitments that matured on October 7, 2026" (page:149), while the $953 million availability is measured at September 30, 2026, before that date. Mechanism: the headline liquidity figure includes a tranche that expired five weeks later, and the sources do not say whether it was extended, replaced or lapsed. Consequence: the liquidity data module must show availability at the balance-sheet date and flag the post-balance-sheet change, and cannot state post-October availability. - Interest cover basis. Evidence: cash paid for interest is printed for FY2025 only (10-K page:163); the interim cash flow statements print only non-cash items in the supplemental section (10-Q Q3 page:6). Mechanism: net interest expense is available for every period, cash interest is not. Consequence: any 2026 interest cover must be labelled as based on interest expense, net, not cash interest. - Covenant headroom. Evidence: a 2.00 to 1.00 maximum is printed (10-K page:211), the Third Amendment is said to have "increased the maximum senior secured net leverage ratio quarterly maintenance test through the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2026" (10-Q Q3 page:25), but neither the temporary level nor the reported ratio is printed. Mechanism: the Credit Agreement definitions of EBITDA and senior secured net debt differ from the Adjusted EBITDA and total debt principal used in the release. Consequence: headroom cannot be computed from the pack and must be written Not calculable. - Revised comparatives. Evidence: prior-period amounts were revised for immaterial errors related primarily to income tax expense timing (10-Q Q3 page:7-8; 10-K page:165). Mechanism: 2025 figures in the 2026 filings differ from the originally reported 2025 filings, which are not in the pack. Consequence: year-over-year and LTM figures must use the revised comparatives and say so.

facts.text: Two statements in the source-readiness handoff are corrected here because that handoff cannot be edited. First, it says the revolving tranche expired "five weeks" after the balance-sheet date; the tranche matured on October 7, 2026, one week after September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:149). Second, its gap 4 describes the depreciation and amortization difference between the Q3 2026 release and the 10-Q loosely; the release page:13 prints nine-month 2025 depreciation and amortization of 236 and restructuring of 54, the 10-Q page:133 prints 259 and 31, and the 23 shifted between the two lines is consistent with the $23 of accelerated depreciation that the 10-K (page:318) places within depreciation and amortization; both lines are added back, so the shift does not change Adjusted EBITDA. The separate difference of 5 in nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA (614 versus 619) remains unexplained by the sources.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is adequate for a leverage, liquidity and maturity review to 2026-09-30, on the stated bases and with named restrictions. Leverage is calculated on Adjusted EBITDA built from the filed segment reconciliation (segment Adjusted EBITDA plus the other non-reportable segment less corporate expenses), because no filing prints a consolidated Adjusted EBITDA; management's own trailing figure is 744 and its net leverage is approximately 4.3x, consistent with the filing-basis 4.25x. The reading is that the issuer has reduced principal by 310 since December 2025 and moved net leverage down by about 0.4x, from a high starting point, with thin book equity and a large claims layer outside debt (environmental remediation, accrued litigation, leases, pensions, supplier and receivable financing). Interest cover is measurable on cash interest only for FY2024 and FY2025. Covenant headroom is Not calculable. The 220 revolver tranche that matured after quarter-end is a subsequent event that the liquidity figure does not reflect.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, implication
facts.text: - Leverage is high and falling slowly, helped by asset sales. Evidence: debt principal fell from 4,182 to 3,872 while nine-month 2026 proceeds from sales of assets were 342 (10-Q Q3 page:5). Mechanism: the reduction comes mainly from euro term loan repayments of EUR 280 million (about 324) in the nine months, partly funded from Kuan Yin land sale proceeds (release Q1 page:4); the March 2026 issue of 700 replaced redemptions of 683 of 2027 and 2028 notes (page:27), so it did not reduce debt. Implication: further deleveraging relies on EBITDA growth (management guides full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 775 to 800, release page:6) and on the cash cost of PFAS settlements, so leverage near 4x is the likely floor without further disposals. - Adjusted EBITDA overstates cash for debt service. Evidence: FY2025 litigation-related charges of 320 and environmental charges of 93 are excluded (10-K page:317), and nine-month 2026 environmental charges of 168 and net litigation charges of 106 are excluded (10-Q Q3 page:133). Mechanism: these are accrued liabilities paid over years, including 100 to New Jersey in September 2026 and 51 to North Carolina in October 2026. Implication: coverage and leverage on Adjusted EBITDA should be read next to reported operating cash flow, which was negative 633 in FY2024 and 264 in FY2025. - Interest burden is steady. Evidence: interest expense, net was 269 for FY2025 and 206 for nine months 2026; the new 7.875% notes replaced 5.375% and 5.750% notes while the term loan margin rose to 3.50% (page:26-27). Mechanism: refinancing at higher coupons offset debt reduction; management expects annual interest expense to fall by only about 3 (page:151). Implication: little interest relief from the deleveraging to date. - Segment mix. Evidence: Q3 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA was 136 in Thermal and Specialized Solutions, 85 in Titanium Technologies and 24 in Advanced Performance Materials against 194, 25 and 14 a year earlier (10-Q Q3 page:133). Mechanism: titanium pricing recovery offsets lower aftermarket refrigerant sales. Implication: the earnings base is more cyclical than the refrigerant franchise alone suggests. - Thin equity. Evidence: total equity of 156 against total liabilities of 7,137 (10-Q Q3 page:3-4). Mechanism: litigation and environmental charges have consumed retained earnings. Implication: book equity gives no cushion and debt capacity rests on cash flow and asset values.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The company is a listed operating business, not a sponsor-owned credit, and there is no acquisition or leveraged buyout in the sources. The transactions that matter are financing, disposal and litigation settlements: a 700 senior notes issue in March 2026 that refinanced shorter notes, repayment of euro term loan principal funded partly by the sale of the Kuan Yin, Taiwan land, a revolver tranche that matured in October 2026, and two large state PFAS settlements. Business risk rests on three segments with different cycles: refrigerants (growth driven by regulation, now reversing from a one-off channel fill), titanium dioxide (a commodity-like pigment where pricing and a concentrated customer base drive earnings) and high-performance materials (smaller, with technology exposure to semiconductors and data centers). Ownership is public with no controlling holder disclosed in the supplied sources. The creditor-relevant change over the period is a lower dividend, lower gross debt after asset sales, higher unrecovered legal obligations, a Moody's downgrade to B1 with a stable outlook, and a continuing audit committee review overhang. Governance evidence is documentary and mixed rather than adverse; legal capacity cannot be assessed without the debt documents.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition, sponsor buyout, dividend recapitalisation or other change of control appears in the supplied sources; transaction type is therefore Insufficient Information as an ownership event and the relevant events are financing, disposal and settlement transactions. The one new debt issue in the period is the 7.875 percent senior notes due 2034, closed on March 12, 2026 in a private offering of 700 aggregate principal amount under the 2020 base indenture and a Fourth Supplemental Indenture, with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee and "the guarantor named therein" (unnamed in the filings); proceeds were 690 net of 10 of fees (10-Q Q3 page:27, page:151; status: completed). The net proceeds, with cash on hand, redeemed 188 of the 5.750 percent senior notes due 2028 for about 190 and all 495 of the 5.375 percent senior notes due 2027 for 499 (page:27), which removed the 2027 maturity and left the 2028 notes at 595. The effect on leverage is neutral because 700 replaced 683 of principal; the effect on the maturity profile is to push 700 to 2034, and management expects annual interest expense to fall only about 3 (page:151, Management Language). Separately, the senior secured Euro term loan due August 2028 was reduced from EUR 415 million to EUR 135 million through repayments of EUR 280 million in the nine months, including EUR 140 million in April 2026 funded partly by Kuan Yin land sale proceeds (release Q1 page:4; 10-Q Q3 page:26). The U.S. dollar term loan had its maturity extended from August 2028 to October 2032 and its margin raised to adjusted Term SOFR plus 3.50 percent under the Fourth Amendment of October 15, 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:25-26, status: executed and in effect), and the Third Amendment of May 2, 2025 raised the revolver to 1,000 commitments with a temporary higher senior secured net leverage test through the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (page:25). Of those commitments, 220 matured on October 7, 2026, a subsequent event before the cutoff that the filings state as fact without saying whether it was extended or replaced (page:149). Liquidity use of proceeds: the Kuan Yin disposal, ten parcels with a purchase price of approximately 360 under January 2026 agreements (10-K page:16), closed with nine parcels in April 2026 for gross proceeds of 300 and net cash of 287, a gain of 266 in Q2 2026, and the tenth in September 2026 for total consideration of 56 and a gain of 50 (10-Q Q3 page:22); management states total net consideration of about 340 (release Q3 page:1). These three measures (agreement price, gross consideration and net consideration) are on different bases and are not a conflict. Litigation settlements are the other transactions: the New Jersey judicial consent order, entered in August 2026 and final in September 2026, sets payments totaling 875 over 25 years shared equally between Chemours and DuPont and Corteva, with 100 paid in September 2026 and the company's remaining share recorded at 176 on a net present value basis (10-Q Q3 page:91); the North Carolina settlement of September 2026 sets overall payments of 455 over 15 years with legal reserves of 205 recorded, and a first annual payment of 51 was made in October 2026, a subsequent event (page:116). The filings do not state whether the 455 is the company's share or the total for all parties. A 2026 Consent Decree with the EPA and the West Virginia environmental authority carries a 23 civil penalty over three years (page:111) and expanded off-site drinking water obligations. All these terms are the company's own descriptions: the executed settlement documents, the indentures and the Credit Agreement are not supplied.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Customer concentration in titanium dioxide. Evidence: ten largest customers over 44 percent and one over 20 percent of segment sales (F3). Mechanic: loss or repricing of one buyer moves segment volume and margin quickly because the product is a commodity-like pigment with a demand base tied to construction and packaging (F7). Implication: segment earnings, which recovered in Q3 2026 on pricing (F6), carry volatility that leverage should be tested against; the portfolio-wide customer breadth (F2) does not remove it. - Refrigerant earnings normalizing. rows.label: Chemours is a listed chemicals producer in three segments, with no sponsor identified. Its credit story is a cyclical, concentrated earnings base carrying large legacy PFAS and environmental obligations, partly shared with DuPont and Corteva.
About 2,400 customers, none above 10 percent of sales, but the ten largest titanium customers exceed 44 percent of that segment and one exceeds 20 percent.
Refrigerant earnings have fallen as the aftermarket channel fill of the prior year reversed, while titanium earnings recovered on pricing.
New Jersey (875 over 25 years) and North Carolina (455 over 15 years) settlements set multi-year cash calls; DuPont and Corteva share half of future legacy PFAS cost.
Behaviour is supportive: the dividend was cut and land sale proceeds repaid debt. Governance carries a 2024 audit committee review and prior-period revisions.
Dividend reduced from 1.00 per share in 2024 to 0.0875 per quarter in 2026; no repurchases
Land sale proceeds applied to euro term loan repayment, with stated intent to reduce debt
Refinancing of 2027 and part of 2028 notes with 2034 notes; term loan extended to 2032
2024 audit committee review, 2023 material weaknesses, revised prior periods, advancement of former senior managers' legal fees
Cost sharing of legacy PFAS liabilities with DuPont and Corteva, including their funding of 150 into escrow
Legal capacity to add debt, make distributions or release collateral
Credit Agreement, amendments, covenant certificate and covenant EBITDA definitions
Executed New Jersey, North Carolina and Consent Decree documents
Cash interest paid for 2026 interim periods

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Chemours is a leveraged, cyclical chemicals credit with adequate near-term liquidity, whose cash flow is increasingly claimed by legacy PFAS settlements. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt principal fell to USD 3,872 million at 2026-09-30, net leverage eased to 4.25x, unrestricted cash was USD 698 million, no revolver amounts were drawn, and DuPont and Corteva share half of future qualifying legacy PFAS cost. The weakest point is that Adjusted EBITDA excludes settlement and environmental cash while book equity is only USD 156 million. What decides the outcome is whether titanium dioxide pricing holds as refrigerant sales normalise, and whether the 2028 and 2029 debt is refinanced before the revolver springing maturity applies.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Deleveraging is the first: total debt principal fell by USD 310 million in the nine months of 2026 to USD 3,872 million, and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA eased from 4.68x at FY2025 to 4.25x at LTM Q3 2026 on the filing basis; management reports about 4.3x on its own basis (Documentary Fact for the debt figures, Analyst Interpretation for the trend; basis CP-1 leverage table, CP-1A F26). The maturity profile is clear until 2028: the 5.375 percent notes due May 2027 were redeemed, and scheduled payments are USD 26 million for the remainder of 2026 and USD 42 million for 2027 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 maturities table). Liquidity at the balance-sheet date was unrestricted cash of USD 698 million and revolver availability of USD 953 million net of letters of credit, with no revolver borrowings, and management states liquidity is adequate through at least the end of November 2027 (Documentary Fact; the horizon is Management Language; basis CP-1 liquidity table, CP-1A F28). The customer base is broad outside titanium: about 2,400 customers in about 110 countries, none above 10 percent of consolidated sales, and none above 10 percent in refrigerants or advanced materials (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F2). DuPont and Corteva bear the other half of qualifying future legacy PFAS cost up to an aggregate USD 4,000 million, with about USD 1,130 million available, and funded USD 150 million into escrow when the New Jersey order became final (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F13, F20). Issuer behaviour is supportive on the documented actions: the dividend fell from USD 1.00 per share declared in 2024 to USD 0.0875 per quarter in 2026, no shares were repurchased, and land sale proceeds funded repayment of the euro term loan (Analyst Interpretation of documented actions; basis CP-1A F24 to F26). Titanium Technologies segment Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 85 million in Q3 2026 from USD 25 million a year earlier on a price increase, and management describes a low-cost chloride process (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the cost position; basis CP-1A F6, F7).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage is high and equity thin: total debt principal over Adjusted EBITDA was 5.18x at LTM Q3 2026, and total equity was USD 156 million against total liabilities of USD 7,137 million, so book value gives no cushion (Documentary Fact; the cushion reading is Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 leverage and financial tables). Adjusted EBITDA overstates the cash available for debt service: it excludes litigation charges of USD 320 million and environmental charges of USD 93 million in FY2025, and USD 106 million and USD 168 million respectively in the nine months of 2026, while reported operating cash flow was negative USD 633 million in FY2024 and USD 264 million in FY2025 (Documentary Fact; the reading is Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 financial table and interpretation). Settlement cash calls are large: New Jersey totals USD 875 million over 25 years with USD 100 million paid in September 2026, North Carolina totals USD 455 million over 15 years with a first payment of USD 51 million in October 2026, and matters for which loss is reasonably possible but not estimable remain unreserved (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F18, F19, F21). Earnings are rotating toward the more cyclical segment: Thermal and Specialized Solutions Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million in Q3 2026 as the prior-year aftermarket channel fill reversed, while the recovery is in titanium (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the channel-fill cause; basis CP-1A F4 to F6). Titanium customers are concentrated: the ten largest exceed 44 percent of segment sales and one exceeds 20 percent (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F3). Interest cover is thin and relief small: Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest was 2.99x in FY2025, and management expects annual interest expense to fall by only about USD 3 million after the 2026 refinancing at higher coupons (Documentary Fact; relief is Management Language; basis CP-1 interest cover table, CP-1A transaction summary). A 2024 audit committee review, 2023 material weaknesses remediated in 2024 and revised prior periods keep a monitoring flag (Documentary Fact; the flag is Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A F14 to F16).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, leverage is high but falling: net debt over Adjusted EBITDA was 4.68x at FY2025 and 4.25x at LTM Q3 2026, and total debt over Adjusted EBITDA 5.58x and 5.18x, on a filing-component basis that sums segment Adjusted EBITDA less corporate expenses (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 leverage table). Second, the refinancing wall begins in 2028: USD 780 million falls in 2028 and USD 647 million in 2029 with USD 2,419 million after 2030, and the revolver has a springing maturity if the term loans or the 2028 and 2029 notes are not repaid or refinanced within 91 days before their maturity (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 maturities and debt schedule). Third, liquidity is adequate at 2026-09-30 but the headline includes a tranche that matured on October 7, 2026: cash of USD 698 million plus availability of USD 953 million, of which USD 220 million of commitments matured, so availability would be USD 733 million if the tranche lapsed (Documentary Fact for the maturity, Analyst Interpretation for the scenario; basis CP-1 liquidity calculation, CP-1A F27). Fourth, settlement obligations are the dominant claim outside debt: recorded reserves include USD 205 million for North Carolina and USD 176 million for New Jersey on a net present value basis, and environmental remediation liabilities total USD 116 million current and USD 689 million non-current (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 claims table, CP-1A F18, F19). Fifth, earnings are rotating from refrigerants to titanium dioxide: Q3 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA was USD 136 million in refrigerants, USD 85 million in titanium and USD 24 million in advanced materials, against USD 194 million, USD 25 million and USD 14 million a year earlier (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F6). Sixth, issuer behaviour toward creditors is supportive on the documented actions (lower dividend, no repurchases, asset sale cash applied to debt), with no priming, uptiering or non-pro-rata exchange in the sources, while legal capacity cannot be assessed (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A governance table, F24 to F26, F30).

rows.label: Chemours is a leveraged, cyclical credit with adequate near-term liquidity, falling debt and cost-shared legacy liabilities, but its cash flow is claimed by multi-year PFAS settlements and book equity is thin.
Total debt principal fell from USD 4,182 million to USD 3,872 million, and net leverage eased from 4.68x to 4.25x between FY2025 and Q3 2026.
The 2028 maturity of USD 780 million and the 2029 maturity of USD 647 million sit within the revolver springing-maturity window.
Settlement obligations to New Jersey and North Carolina are multi-year cash calls that Adjusted EBITDA excludes.
Refrigerant earnings are falling as the prior-year channel fill reverses, while titanium earnings recover on pricing and rely on a concentrated customer base.
Legacy PFAS and environmental cash calls
Regulatory and litigation exposure from the audit committee review

facts.label: Confidence score
facts.text: Formula: score equals (0.6 times E plus 0.4 times C) times S less P, clamped to 0 to 100. E is the mean strongest lineage weight over 18 material claims: 12 Directly Sourced at 1.0, 3 Calculated at 0.9, 1 Assumption-Based at 0.5 and 2 Analyst Inference at 0.4, giving 88.89. C is 17 required registers present of 17, giving 100. S is 1.0 (source gate pass). P is 15 for one MATERIAL finding plus 24 for eight MINOR findings, giving 39. Score equals (0.6 times 88.89 plus 40) times 1.0 less 39, or 54.33, rounded to 54. A MATERIAL finding caps the score at 59 and sets Restricted; 54 is below the cap and falls in the Low band (40 to 59).

### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

All four downstream modules can run, each with bounded gaps. | Medium | No credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so covenant tests, guarantors and the revolver after its October 2026 maturity are not verifiable. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| A $220 million revolving tranche matured on October 7, 2026, after the balance-sheet date, and the sources do not say whether it was extended or replaced. | Reported availability of $953 million may overstate liquidity after that date. | Medium |
| Interim cash interest paid is not printed; only FY2025 shows it. | A cash-basis interest cover for the last twelve months to Q3 2026 cannot be built from the pack. | High |

| The covenant level is printed only as a 2.00 to 1.00 maximum senior secured net leverage ratio, with no reported ratio or headroom. | Covenant headroom needs the Credit Agreement definitions, which are not supplied. | High |

| Prior-year amounts were revised, and one prior-period Adjusted EBITDA figure does not tie between the filing components and the release. | Period comparisons need a stated basis and a documented conflict. | Medium |
### Readiness view

Source sufficiency is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four selected consumers: the financial data and ratio module (CP-1), the business and transaction context module (CP-1A), the fundamental credit synthesis (CP-2) and the evidence-trace validator (CP-5). No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, because no missing source prevents any consumer's own method and no critical identity boundary is unresolved: the reporting entity is the consolidated registrant, named identically on the cover of every filing. The limitations below are carried into each consumer and are source gaps, not findings about downstream analysis, which is not yet done.
### Coverage of the requested work
| Evidence need | Located in the pack | Assessment |
| Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, equity | 10-K pages 160-162; 10-Q Q3 pages 2-6 (nine-month and three-month; balance sheet at 2026-09-30 versus 2025-12-31) | Adequate; filed |

### Source-by-source assessment

- **10-K FY2025.** Entity: The Chemours Company, Commission File Number 001-36794 (page:1). Covers three years of statements (page:160-162), debt Note 20 (page:208), commitments and contingent liabilities Note 22 (page:221), long-term employee benefits Note 27 (page:307), supplemental cash flow Note 28 (page:313, cash and restricted cash reconciliation; cash paid for interest and taxes at page:163) and segment Note 29 (page:314). It carries the revision of previously issued financial statements (page:165). Quote at page:211: "maximum senior secured net leverage ratio of 2.00 to 1.00".

- **10-Q Q1 2026.** Same entity; three months ended 2026-03-31. Debt Note 15 at page:19, liquidity at page:124, segments at page:110. The debt maturities paragraph at page:24 states "The Company is not required to make additional principal payments in 2025", which sits oddly in a 2026 filing; the Q2 and Q3 filings say 2026 (page:29 and page:30). Treated as a wording inconsistency, not a conflict of figures.

- **10-Q Q2 2026.** Same entity; three and six months ended 2026-06-30. Debt Note 15 at page:23, liquidity at page:135, segments at page:119. At page:136 it records Moody's downgrade to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026.

- **10-Q Q3 2026.** Same entity; three and nine months ended 2026-09-30; 150,534,489 shares outstanding at November 2, 2026 (page:1). Income statement page:2 (net sales $1,540 for the quarter and $4,512 for nine months), balance sheet page:3, cash flow pages 5-6, debt Note 15 pages 23-30, segments pages 130-133, liquidity pages 148-151. Footnote on page:2: SG&A includes "$150 received by the Company related to the PFAS Insurance MOU".

- **Releases.** Each release is a management summary of one quarter with a non-GAAP reconciliation (Q3: pages 12-13). They give Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income, free cash flow, a net leverage ratio of approximately 4.3x and a Full Year 2026 Outlook (pages 5-6). Attributed management claims only; the net leverage ratio is management's definition (total debt principal less unrestricted cash over Adjusted EBITDA).
### Source-risk mechanisms and downstream consequences

- **Revolver maturity.** Evidence: the 10-Q states "$220 million in revolving commitments that matured on October 7, 2026" (page:149), while the $953 million availability is measured at September 30, 2026, before that date. Mechanism: the headline liquidity figure includes a tranche that expired five weeks later, and the sources do not say whether it was extended, replaced or lapsed. Consequence: the liquidity data module must show availability at the balance-sheet date and flag the post-balance-sheet change, and cannot state post-October availability.

- **Interest cover basis.** Evidence: cash paid for interest is printed for FY2025 only (10-K page:163); the interim cash flow statements print only non-cash items in the supplemental section (10-Q Q3 page:6). Mechanism: net interest expense is available for every period, cash interest is not. Consequence: any 2026 interest cover must be labelled as based on interest expense, net, not cash interest.

- **Covenant headroom.** Evidence: a 2.00 to 1.00 maximum is printed (10-K page:211), the Third Amendment is said to have "increased the maximum senior secured net leverage ratio quarterly maintenance test through the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2026" (10-Q Q3 page:25), but neither the temporary level nor the reported ratio is printed. Mechanism: the Credit Agreement definitions of EBITDA and senior secured net debt differ from the Adjusted EBITDA and total debt principal used in the release. Consequence: headroom cannot be computed from the pack and must be written Not calculable.

- **Revised comparatives.** Evidence: prior-period amounts were revised for immaterial errors related primarily to income tax expense timing (10-Q Q3 page:7-8; 10-K page:165). Mechanism: 2025 figures in the 2026 filings differ from the originally reported 2025 filings, which are not in the pack. Consequence: year-over-year and LTM figures must use the revised comparatives and say so.
## Calculations
No new analytical calculation is made in this module. The checks below only test whether printed figures tie, to find source conflicts; their results are not normalized figures.

| Three months 2025 Adjusted EBITDA from 10-Q components | 233, 2, (45); 10-Q Q3 page:133 | 233 + 2 - 45 = 190 | Release prints 189. Differs by 1. |
| Net debt tie-out | Total debt principal 3,872 less unrestricted cash 698; 10-Q Q3 page:24 and page:149 | 3,872 - 698 = 3,174 | Release page:13 prints 3,174. Ties. |

| Liquidity tie-out | Cash 698 plus revolver availability 953 (1,000 commitments less 47 letters of credit); 10-Q Q3 page:149, page:26 | 698 + 953 = 1,651 | Release page:4 prints "$1.7 billion". Ties after rounding. |
| Restricted cash tie-out | Current 41 plus non-current 62; 10-Q Q3 page:3 | 41 + 62 = 103 | Release page:2 footnote: "Restricted cash approximated $103 million". Ties. |

The two Adjusted EBITDA differences are logged as a conflict in Gaps. The 10-Q does not print a consolidated Adjusted EBITDA total, so the 10-Q-side totals above are sums of printed components, not printed figures.

Level printed: 2.00 to 1.00. | High | Financial data, synthesis | 10-K page:211; 10-Q Q3 page:25, page:149 | Obtain the Credit Agreement and Amendments 1-4. Until then write Not calculable. |

FY2025 printed. | Medium | Financial data (interest cover) | 10-K page:163; absent from 10-Q Q1, Q2 and Q3 supplemental cash flow (Q3 page:6, page:129) | Label interest cover as based on interest expense, net; request the interim cash interest data. |

| 4 | Conflict: nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is 614 in the Q3 2026 release and 619 as the sum of printed 10-Q components; three-month 2025 is 189 versus 190. The same release prints 2025 depreciation and amortization of 236 for nine months while the 10-Q prints 239 for 2026 and 259 for 2025 (page:133), and restructuring of 54 versus 31, so definitions differ between documents. | Medium | Financial data (LTM EBITDA, leverage trend), trace | Release page:13; 10-Q Q3 page:133 | Do not choose or average. Quote both, use the filing for statement lines and the release only as an attributed management measure, and let the next module disclose its basis. |

Run the financial data and ratio module (CP-1) next, then the business and transaction context module (CP-1A), then the fundamental credit synthesis (CP-2), then the evidence-trace validator (CP-5). Each is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and must carry the gaps above: report availability at 2026-09-30 and flag the October 7, 2026 maturity; state interest cover on interest expense, net, because 2026 cash interest is not printed; write covenant headroom as Not calculable; use revised 2025 comparatives; quote both sides of the 2025 Adjusted EBITDA conflict; and keep management ratios attributed. Two statements in the source-readiness handoff are corrected here because that handoff cannot be edited. | At 2026-09-30 total debt principal was 3,872 against unrestricted cash of 698, or 5.18x gross and 4.25x net of Adjusted EBITDA of 747 on the filing basis. Leverage has eased since FY2025 but remains high, with equity of only 156. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDA is not printed as a consolidated filing total, 2026 cash interest is not printed, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated. |

| Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of 698 plus revolver availability of 953, but a 220 tranche of the revolver matured on October 7, 2026. | Liquidity after October is lower than the headline unless the tranche was extended, which the sources do not say. | Medium |

| The largest maturities are 780 in 2028 and 647 in 2029, and the revolver has a springing maturity tied to those refinancings. | Refinancing of the 2028 euro term loan and notes is the key funding event; 2,419 falls after 2030. | High |

| Adjusted EBITDA excludes large litigation and environmental charges, and cash settlement payments are running alongside, including 100 paid to New Jersey in September 2026. | Adjusted EBITDA overstates cash available for debt service; reported cash flow from operations is the better test. | Medium |
| Interest cover can be built on cash interest only for FY2024 and FY2025, at 2.94x and 2.99x. | Current cash interest cover is not measurable from the filings. | High |
### Financial base view

The financial base is adequate for a leverage, liquidity and maturity review to 2026-09-30, on the stated bases and with named restrictions. Leverage is calculated on Adjusted EBITDA built from the filed segment reconciliation (segment Adjusted EBITDA plus the other non-reportable segment less corporate expenses), because no filing prints a consolidated Adjusted EBITDA; management's own trailing figure is 744 and its net leverage is approximately 4.3x, consistent with the filing-basis 4.25x. The reading is that the issuer has reduced principal by 310 since December 2025 and moved net leverage down by about 0.4x, from a high starting point, with thin book equity and a large claims layer outside debt (environmental remediation, accrued litigation, leases, pensions, supplier and receivable financing). Interest cover is measurable on cash interest only for FY2024 and FY2025. Covenant headroom is Not calculable. The 220 revolver tranche that matured after quarter-end is a subsequent event that the liquidity figure does not reflect.
### Chart data: leverage

Total other operating expenses are the sum of printed lines: FY2025 799 plus 108 plus 59; nine months 2026 591 plus 77 plus 19; Q3 2026 negative 25 plus 24 plus 3. Nine-month 2026 other income of 347 compares with 23 a year earlier in a period where the segment reconciliation shows a gain on asset sales of 316 (10-Q Q3 page:133). Income taxes of 307 on pre-tax income of 200 for the nine months (page:2) mean net income stays negative despite positive pre-tax income; the release's Adjusted Net Income reconciliation adds back adjustments made to income taxes of 209 for the nine months (release page:13).
### Interpretation: evidence, mechanism, implication

- **Leverage is high and falling slowly, helped by asset sales.** Evidence: debt principal fell from 4,182 to 3,872 while nine-month 2026 proceeds from sales of assets were 342 (10-Q Q3 page:5). Mechanism: the reduction comes mainly from euro term loan repayments of EUR 280 million (about 324) in the nine months, partly funded from Kuan Yin land sale proceeds (release Q1 page:4); the March 2026 issue of 700 replaced redemptions of 683 of 2027 and 2028 notes (page:27), so it did not reduce debt. Implication: further deleveraging relies on EBITDA growth (management guides full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of 775 to 800, release page:6) and on the cash cost of PFAS settlements, so leverage near 4x is the likely floor without further disposals.

- **Adjusted EBITDA overstates cash for debt service.** Evidence: FY2025 litigation-related charges of 320 and environmental charges of 93 are excluded (10-K page:317), and nine-month 2026 environmental charges of 168 and net litigation charges of 106 are excluded (10-Q Q3 page:133). Mechanism: these are accrued liabilities paid over years, including 100 to New Jersey in September 2026 and 51 to North Carolina in October 2026. Implication: coverage and leverage on Adjusted EBITDA should be read next to reported operating cash flow, which was negative 633 in FY2024 and 264 in FY2025.

- **Interest burden is steady.** Evidence: interest expense, net was 269 for FY2025 and 206 for nine months 2026; the new 7.875% notes replaced 5.375% and 5.750% notes while the term loan margin rose to 3.50% (page:26-27). Mechanism: refinancing at higher coupons offset debt reduction; management expects annual interest expense to fall by only about 3 (page:151). Implication: little interest relief from the deleveraging to date.

- **Segment mix.** Evidence: Q3 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA was 136 in Thermal and Specialized Solutions, 85 in Titanium Technologies and 24 in Advanced Performance Materials against 194, 25 and 14 a year earlier (10-Q Q3 page:133). Mechanism: titanium pricing recovery offsets lower aftermarket refrigerant sales. Implication: the earnings base is more cyclical than the refrigerant franchise alone suggests.

- **Thin equity.** Evidence: total equity of 156 against total liabilities of 7,137 (10-Q Q3 page:3-4). Mechanism: litigation and environmental charges have consumed retained earnings. Implication: book equity gives no cushion and debt capacity rests on cash flow and asset values.

LTM interest expense, net to Q3 2026 equals 269 plus 206 less 201, giving 274, which equals the release figure (page:13).
### Liquidity

2026-09-30: unrestricted cash 698 plus revolver availability 953 equals 1,651, against management total liquidity of 1.7 billion (release page:4). Availability 953 equals commitments 1,000 less letters of credit 47. 2025-12-31: 670 plus 955 equals 1,625. 2026-03-31: 563 plus 953 equals 1,516. 2026-06-30: 671 plus 953 equals 1,624. If the 220 tranche matured without replacement, availability would be 780 less 47, or 733, and liquidity 1,431 on 2026-09-30 balances; this is a scenario, not a reported figure, and the sources do not say whether the tranche was extended.
### Cash flow and other tie-outs

Cash from operations less capital expenditure: FY2024 negative 633 less 360 is negative 993; FY2025 264 less 213 is 51; nine months 2025 127 less 168 is negative 41; nine months 2026 263 less 144 is 119; Q3 2026 149 less 51 is 98. Debt principal change: 3,872 less 4,182 is negative 310. Components of 3,872: 1,041 plus 153 plus 595 plus 620 plus 600 plus 700 plus 43 plus 91 plus 12 plus 17. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Chemours is a listed chemicals producer in three segments, with no sponsor identified. Its credit story is a cyclical, concentrated earnings base carrying large legacy PFAS and environmental obligations, partly shared with DuPont and Corteva. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture or settlement document is supplied, so legal capacity and obligation terms rest on the company's own summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| About 2,400 customers, none above 10 percent of sales, but the ten largest titanium customers exceed 44 percent of that segment and one exceeds 20 percent. | Customer breadth in refrigerants and materials offsets concentration in titanium dioxide. | High |

| Refrigerant earnings have fallen as the aftermarket channel fill of the prior year reversed, while titanium earnings recovered on pricing. | Earnings mix is shifting from the strongest franchise to the most cyclical one. | Medium |

| New Jersey (875 over 25 years) and North Carolina (455 over 15 years) settlements set multi-year cash calls; DuPont and Corteva share half of future legacy PFAS cost. | Cash calls compete with debt service for a decade or more; the sharing arrangement limits but does not remove them. | Medium |

| Behaviour is supportive: the dividend was cut and land sale proceeds repaid debt. Governance carries a 2024 audit committee review and prior-period revisions. | Capital allocation favours creditors, but control and disclosure history warrants monitoring. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The company is a listed operating business, not a sponsor-owned credit, and there is no acquisition or leveraged buyout in the sources. The transactions that matter are financing, disposal and litigation settlements: a 700 senior notes issue in March 2026 that refinanced shorter notes, repayment of euro term loan principal funded partly by the sale of the Kuan Yin, Taiwan land, a revolver tranche that matured in October 2026, and two large state PFAS settlements. Business risk rests on three segments with different cycles: refrigerants (growth driven by regulation, now reversing from a one-off channel fill), titanium dioxide (a commodity-like pigment where pricing and a concentrated customer base drive earnings) and high-performance materials (smaller, with technology exposure to semiconductors and data centers). Ownership is public with no controlling holder disclosed in the supplied sources. The creditor-relevant change over the period is a lower dividend, lower gross debt after asset sales, higher unrecovered legal obligations, a Moody's downgrade to B1 with a stable outlook, and a continuing audit committee review overhang. ### Credit translations

- **Customer concentration in titanium dioxide.** Evidence: ten largest customers over 44 percent and one over 20 percent of segment sales (F3). Mechanic: loss or repricing of one buyer moves segment volume and margin quickly because the product is a commodity-like pigment with a demand base tied to construction and packaging (F7). Implication: segment earnings, which recovered in Q3 2026 on pricing (F6), carry volatility that leverage should be tested against; the portfolio-wide customer breadth (F2) does not remove it.

- **Refrigerant earnings normalizing.** Evidence: the large rise in Opteon sales in FY2025 (F4) and the Q3 2026 decline attributed to lower aftermarket sales against elevated prior-year demand (F5, F6). Mechanic: a regulatory transition filled distribution channels once, so growth is front-loaded and the following years show a destocking air pocket. Implication: the strongest segment's earnings are falling while the weakest recovers, so the group earnings base is less stable than the segment margins suggest. Counter-evidence: management cites data center and semiconductor demand growth in the materials segment (release Q3 page:1).

- **Legacy obligations compete with debt service.** Evidence: the New Jersey and North Carolina settlements and the 2026 Consent Decree (F18, F19, F22), with 100 paid in September 2026 and 51 in October 2026. Mechanic: scheduled annual payments over 25 and 15 years are fixed cash calls recorded as accrued litigation at net present value, partly shielded by the cost-sharing MOU with a remaining cap (F13). Implication: free cash flow after settlements, not Adjusted EBITDA, is the relevant coverage test, and the recorded reserves do not cover matters judged reasonably possible but not estimable (F21).

- **Control and disclosure history.** Evidence: F14, F15, F16. Mechanic: restatement-type revisions and regulatory inquiries raise the risk of further adjustments and costs. Implication: a monitoring flag, not an adverse conclusion, because the revisions were assessed as immaterial and the weaknesses were remediated.

- **Near-term liquidity.** Evidence: availability of 953 included the 220 tranche that matured on October 7, 2026 (F27). Mechanic: the headline liquidity is reduced if the tranche lapsed, leaving 780 of commitments due in 2030 with a springing maturity linked to the 2028 and 2029 debt (F27). Implication: the 2028 refinancing must be addressed within the revolver's springing window; management's stated liquidity horizon is November 2027 (F28).

It moves trailing Adjusted EBITDA by about the same 5, and the financial base states the basis it used. It counters any credit translation that relies on the precision of the earnings trend. The Kuan Yin figures (agreement price of about 360, gross consideration of 300 plus 56, and management's net consideration of about 340) are on different bases and are not a conflict.

### Credit view

Chemours is a leveraged, cyclical chemicals credit with adequate near-term liquidity, whose cash flow is increasingly claimed by legacy PFAS settlements. The strongest support is deleveraging: total debt principal fell to USD 3,872 million at 2026-09-30, net leverage eased to 4.25x, unrestricted cash was USD 698 million, no revolver amounts were drawn, and DuPont and Corteva share half of future qualifying legacy PFAS cost. The weakest point is that Adjusted EBITDA excludes settlement and environmental cash while book equity is only USD 156 million. What decides the outcome is whether titanium dioxide pricing holds as refrigerant sales normalise, and whether the 2028 and 2029 debt is refinanced before the revolver springing maturity applies.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Content |
| Fundamental credit view | Leveraged and cash-constrained, with adequate near-term liquidity and credible deleveraging: financial risk is elevated and business risk is moderate but cyclical |
| Category | Analyst Interpretation |

| Basis | CP-1 leverage, liquidity and maturity tables and debt schedule; CP-1A F2, F3, F6, F13, F18, F19, F24 to F27 and its credit translations |
### Thesis

Deleveraging and cost-sharing of legacy PFAS liabilities support the credit, but cyclical earnings, a concentrated titanium customer base and multi-year settlement cash calls leave leverage near 4x with little margin for error.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Deleveraging is the first: total debt principal fell by USD 310 million in the nine months of 2026 to USD 3,872 million, and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA eased from 4.68x at FY2025 to 4.25x at LTM Q3 2026 on the filing basis; management reports about 4.3x on its own basis (Documentary Fact for the debt figures, Analyst Interpretation for the trend; basis CP-1 leverage table, CP-1A F26). The maturity profile is clear until 2028: the 5.375 percent notes due May 2027 were redeemed, and scheduled payments are USD 26 million for the remainder of 2026 and USD 42 million for 2027 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 maturities table). Liquidity at the balance-sheet date was unrestricted cash of USD 698 million and revolver availability of USD 953 million net of letters of credit, with no revolver borrowings, and management states liquidity is adequate through at least the end of November 2027 (Documentary Fact; the horizon is Management Language; basis CP-1 liquidity table, CP-1A F28). The customer base is broad outside titanium: about 2,400 customers in about 110 countries, none above 10 percent of consolidated sales, and none above 10 percent in refrigerants or advanced materials (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F2). DuPont and Corteva bear the other half of qualifying future legacy PFAS cost up to an aggregate USD 4,000 million, with about USD 1,130 million available, and funded USD 150 million into escrow when the New Jersey order became final (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F13, F20). Issuer behaviour is supportive on the documented actions: the dividend fell from USD 1.00 per share declared in 2024 to USD 0.0875 per quarter in 2026, no shares were repurchased, and land sale proceeds funded repayment of the euro term loan (Analyst Interpretation of documented actions; basis CP-1A F24 to F26). Titanium Technologies segment Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 85 million in Q3 2026 from USD 25 million a year earlier on a price increase, and management describes a low-cost chloride process (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the cost position; basis CP-1A F6, F7).

Weaknesses. Leverage is high and equity thin: total debt principal over Adjusted EBITDA was 5.18x at LTM Q3 2026, and total equity was USD 156 million against total liabilities of USD 7,137 million, so book value gives no cushion (Documentary Fact; the cushion reading is Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 leverage and financial tables). Adjusted EBITDA overstates the cash available for debt service: it excludes litigation charges of USD 320 million and environmental charges of USD 93 million in FY2025, and USD 106 million and USD 168 million respectively in the nine months of 2026, while reported operating cash flow was negative USD 633 million in FY2024 and USD 264 million in FY2025 (Documentary Fact; the reading is Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 financial table and interpretation). Settlement cash calls are large: New Jersey totals USD 875 million over 25 years with USD 100 million paid in September 2026, North Carolina totals USD 455 million over 15 years with a first payment of USD 51 million in October 2026, and matters for which loss is reasonably possible but not estimable remain unreserved (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F18, F19, F21). Earnings are rotating toward the more cyclical segment: Thermal and Specialized Solutions Adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million in Q3 2026 as the prior-year aftermarket channel fill reversed, while the recovery is in titanium (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the channel-fill cause; basis CP-1A F4 to F6). Titanium customers are concentrated: the ten largest exceed 44 percent of segment sales and one exceeds 20 percent (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F3). Interest cover is thin and relief small: Adjusted EBITDA over cash interest was 2.99x in FY2025, and management expects annual interest expense to fall by only about USD 3 million after the 2026 refinancing at higher coupons (Documentary Fact; relief is Management Language; basis CP-1 interest cover table, CP-1A transaction summary). A 2024 audit committee review, 2023 material weaknesses remediated in 2024 and revised prior periods keep a monitoring flag (Documentary Fact; the flag is Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A F14 to F16).
### Key findings

First, leverage is high but falling: net debt over Adjusted EBITDA was 4.68x at FY2025 and 4.25x at LTM Q3 2026, and total debt over Adjusted EBITDA 5.58x and 5.18x, on a filing-component basis that sums segment Adjusted EBITDA less corporate expenses (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1 leverage table). Second, the refinancing wall begins in 2028: USD 780 million falls in 2028 and USD 647 million in 2029 with USD 2,419 million after 2030, and the revolver has a springing maturity if the term loans or the 2028 and 2029 notes are not repaid or refinanced within 91 days before their maturity (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 maturities and debt schedule). Third, liquidity is adequate at 2026-09-30 but the headline includes a tranche that matured on October 7, 2026: cash of USD 698 million plus availability of USD 953 million, of which USD 220 million of commitments matured, so availability would be USD 733 million if the tranche lapsed (Documentary Fact for the maturity, Analyst Interpretation for the scenario; basis CP-1 liquidity calculation, CP-1A F27). Fourth, settlement obligations are the dominant claim outside debt: recorded reserves include USD 205 million for North Carolina and USD 176 million for New Jersey on a net present value basis, and environmental remediation liabilities total USD 116 million current and USD 689 million non-current (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 claims table, CP-1A F18, F19). Fifth, earnings are rotating from refrigerants to titanium dioxide: Q3 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA was USD 136 million in refrigerants, USD 85 million in titanium and USD 24 million in advanced materials, against USD 194 million, USD 25 million and USD 14 million a year earlier (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A F6). Sixth, issuer behaviour toward creditors is supportive on the documented actions (lower dividend, no repurchases, asset sale cash applied to debt), with no priming, uptiering or non-pro-rata exchange in the sources, while legal capacity cannot be assessed (Analyst Interpretation; basis CP-1A governance table, F24 to F26, F30).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Legacy PFAS and environmental cash calls | Fixed annual settlement payments over 25 and 15 years, a consent decree penalty and drinking water programs are paid from cash that Adjusted EBITDA excludes, and unreserved matters remain reasonably possible but not estimable | Free cash flow after settlements, not Adjusted EBITDA, is the relevant coverage test; adverse developments would erode liquidity and leverage progress; cost sharing with DuPont and Corteva limits but does not remove the exposure | Critical |

| Refinancing of 2028 and 2029 debt | USD 780 million due in 2028 and USD 647 million in 2029 trigger the revolver springing maturity if not refinanced in the 91-day window | A failure to refinance on acceptable terms would remove revolver access at the time it is most needed; ratings of B1 with a stable outlook constrain market access | Material |

| Revolver tranche matured October 7, 2026 | The USD 220 million tranche was part of the USD 953 million availability, and extension or replacement is not stated | Post-quarter liquidity may be lower than the headline; a USD 733 million availability scenario results if it lapsed | Material |

| Earnings cyclicality and mix | Refrigerant earnings normalise after a regulatory channel fill, while titanium earnings depend on pricing and a concentrated customer base | A weak titanium year or further refrigerant decline would raise leverage; management guides fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 160 million to USD 185 million (attributed) | Material |

| Covenant headroom not verifiable | A maximum senior secured net leverage ratio of 2.00x applies to the revolver, the raised temporary level and the reported ratio are not printed, and the Credit Agreement definitions are not supplied | Headroom may be narrower or wider than management's statement of compliance implies | Material |

| Regulatory and litigation exposure from the audit committee review | Regulatory inquiries and private litigation may produce unquantified costs and indemnification advances | Unquantified cash and reputational costs; a monitoring item, not an adverse conclusion | Minor |

| Interest burden | New 7.875 percent notes and a term loan margin of 3.50 percent replaced lower-cost debt, so interest expense falls only slightly with lower principal | Interest cover stays near 3x on Adjusted EBITDA before settlement cash | Minor |
## Calculations
No new calculation is made. Every figure repeats a row of the financial base or the business-context register. Tie-outs of the figures used:
- Debt principal change: USD 3,872 million less USD 4,182 million equals negative USD 310 million (CP-1 debt schedule).
- Net leverage: USD 3,174 million of net debt over USD 747 million of LTM Adjusted EBITDA equals 4.25x; USD 3,512 million over USD 750 million equals 4.68x (CP-1 leverage table).
- Availability scenario: USD 780 million less USD 47 million of letters of credit equals USD 733 million (CP-1 liquidity calculation).
- Segment Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA: USD 136 million plus USD 85 million plus USD 24 million equals USD 245 million (CP-1A calculations).
## Gaps
| # | Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| 1 | Covenant ratio, the raised temporary level and Credit Agreement definitions are not supplied | Headroom cannot be calculated; it governs revolver access | Liquidity and covenant risk rows | High | Obtain the Credit Agreement and amendments; until then headroom is Not calculable |

| 2 | Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026 interim periods | Cash interest cover is measurable only for FY2024 and FY2025 | Interest burden | Medium | Use interest expense, net as a labelled substitute |

| 3 | The USD 220 million revolver tranche that matured on October 7, 2026 has no stated extension or replacement | Post-quarter liquidity is uncertain | Liquidity strength and risk | High | Treat as a subsequent event; no source after the cutoff is usable |

| 4 | Legal capacity (debt baskets, restricted payments, priming, collateral release) is Insufficient Information because the Credit Agreement and indentures are not supplied | Behaviour is assessed from actions only | Governance reading | High | Obtain the debt documents |

| 5 | Ownership and control rights are Insufficient Information; no holder table is in the sources | Alignment between owners and creditors cannot be assessed | Governance reading | Low | Obtain the proxy statement |

| 6 | Executed settlement documents are not supplied, and the USD 455 million North Carolina total is not stated as company share or all-party total | Obligation timing and acceleration terms rest on company summaries | Settlement risk | Medium | Treat the recorded reserve of USD 205 million as the company obligation |

| 7 | Nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA differs between the release (USD 614 million) and the sum of 10-Q components (USD 619 million) | Trend precision of trailing earnings | Leverage trend | Medium | Quote both; the financial base states its basis |
| 8 | The business-context handoff judges this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Confidence cannot be High | Assessment confidence | Medium | Carry the limitations above |
## Next module

Run the evidence-trace validator (CP-5) next. It should open the locators behind the figures in this handoff, particularly the leverage and liquidity rows of the financial base, the settlement terms (New Jersey, North Carolina, 2026 Consent Decree), the revolver maturity and the segment Adjusted EBITDA comparison, and flag management-attributed items for separate treatment.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The figures in the four handoffs trace to filed sources with one wrong page reference and a few labelling slips. Committee use is restricted because covenant headroom and legal capacity cannot be traced to governing documents. | Medium | No credit agreement, indenture or settlement document is supplied, so covenant and structural claims rest on company statements. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Of 18 material claims, 12 are directly sourced, 3 are calculated, 1 is assumption-based and 2 are analyst inference; all stated figures reproduced from the cited pages. | Debt, cash, liquidity and settlement figures can be relied on as filed facts. | High |

| Compliance with the revolver covenant is a management statement only; the tested level and the reported ratio are not printed. | Headroom on the revolver is unverified, which restricts any conclusion on revolver access. | High |
| Leverage on the carrying value of debt is 5.13x gross and 4.20x net, against 5.18x and 4.25x on principal. | The basis choice moves leverage by about 0.05x and does not change the view. | High |
| Eight minor defects were found, two of them wording errors already corrected downstream. | None changes a figure; they are logged for clean-up. | High |
### Evidence trace view

The traced evidence is sound for the stated purpose of a fundamental, filings-based credit screen. Every dollar figure in the financial base, the business context and the synthesis was found on the cited page of the cited filing or release, except one locator that points to the wrong page and one row whose composition is inferred rather than printed. Calculated figures reproduce from their printed inputs. The weaknesses are in what the sources cannot show: the covenant test, the guarantee and security structure, the status of the revolving tranche that matured on October 7, 2026, cash interest for 2026, and the executed settlement documents. Because those gaps bear on committee conclusions about revolver access and legal capacity, the research is graded Restricted, not Passed, and the synthesis confidence of Medium is appropriate.
### Traceability conclusion

The analysis is traceable enough for a fundamental credit screen but not for covenant, legal-structure or relative-value decisions. Supported claims dominate: the debt schedule, liquidity, maturity profile, segment results and settlement terms all reproduce from filed pages, and derived leverage and cover ratios recompute from printed inputs. Inference is confined to labelled interpretation, such as the earnings rotation and the supportive reading of issuer behaviour, and one labelled scenario for revolver availability. The most important provenance gap is the missing Credit Agreement: management states covenant compliance, but neither the tested level after the temporary relief nor the reported ratio can be traced. The remediation is to obtain the Credit Agreement, its amendments and the latest compliance certificate.

## Calculations
All amounts in USD millions. Inputs are from the cited pages; results were recomputed in this module.
### Debt basis check

Balance-sheet carrying debt at 2026-09-30 is current maturities 50 plus long-term debt 3,783, giving 3,833 (10-Q Q3 page:3). Total debt principal is 3,872, so the gap is 39, equal to unamortized discounts of 15 plus issuance costs of 24 (page:24). On carrying value, total debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 747 is 5.13x and net debt (3,833 less 698, or 3,135) over 747 is 4.20x. At 2025-12-31: carrying debt 42 plus 4,099 equals 4,141, against principal of 4,182, a gap of 41 (discounts 21 plus costs 20); 4,141 over 750 is 5.52x and (4,141 less 670, or 3,471) over 750 is 4.63x.
### Adjusted EBITDA basis check

On the release trailing figure of 744 for Q3 2026, principal over EBITDA is 3,872 over 744, or 5.20x, and net is 3,174 over 744, or 4.27x, against 5.18x and 4.25x on the filing basis; the basis moves each ratio by 0.02x.
### Locator audit

Fifty-eight locator-and-value checks were run on the source text: page and figure for debt, cash, equity, letters of credit, segment reconciliations, settlement terms, ratings, release reconciliations and the Q1 and Q2 positions. Fifty-seven matched. The one miss is the dividends-paid line, on page:6 and not page:5 (I-02).
### Confidence score

Formula: score equals (0.6 times E plus 0.4 times C) times S less P, clamped to 0 to 100. E is the mean strongest lineage weight over 18 material claims: 12 Directly Sourced at 1.0, 3 Calculated at 0.9, 1 Assumption-Based at 0.5 and 2 Analyst Inference at 0.4, giving 88.89. C is 17 required registers present of 17, giving 100. S is 1.0 (source gate pass). P is 15 for one MATERIAL finding plus 24 for eight MINOR findings, giving 39. Score equals (0.6 times 88.89 plus 40) times 1.0 less 39, or 54.33, rounded to 54. A MATERIAL finding caps the score at 59 and sets Restricted; 54 is below the cap and falls in the Low band (40 to 59).
